Hi Olivia — appreciate the clear list. Attaching a short decision matrix and a one-page cheat sheet for private offers. Below is a concise summary I recommend you include in the procurement packet.

Executive summary (pilot vs long-term):
- Pilot (recommended): AWS Marketplace private offer — fastest PO closure (purchase order + private offer), fixed billing entity through AWS, minimal legal review on our side, can be provisioned same day after PO. Good when procurement wants predictable invoicing and quick start.
- Long-term/Enterprise (recommended later): Direct contract (MSA + SOW) — better for custom SLAs, bespoke termination/indemnity clauses, and volume discounts. Requires procurement and legal review; expect a 3–6 week cycle for MSA negotiation.

Risk/reward highlights:
- Time-to-launch: marketplace < direct (hours–days vs weeks).
- Pricing flexibility: direct > marketplace (we can offer negotiated credits/discounts).
- Co-sell credits: via marketplace co-sell programs you may see different partner-crediting windows; direct deals enable clearer co-sell attrib and larger partner incentives in most cases.
- Revenue recognition/billing: marketplace invoices come from AWS (customer pays AWS), which simplifies PO routing but may change your vendor ledger entry; direct invoices come from Redwood and are reflected directly as vendor AR from Redwood.
- Audit/evidence: both paths support SOC2 evidence; private offers still allow customer-controlled terms for data handling, but proofs (audit logs) are provided through our platform regardless of route.

Attachments: procurement_channel_matrix.xlsx (matrix + recommended language), redwood_private_offer_cheatsheet.pdf (how private offers appear on an approval form). I also attached a COA/SOW template for finance if you think the pilot will need an SOW.

Suggested next steps:
1) If procurement wants the fastest path, start with a private offer and we’ll prepare the private offer quote.
2) If procurement insists on Redwood invoicing, request a standard PO and we’ll route to our finance/SDR team for a direct invoice quote; allow ~10 business days for PO acceptance and setup.
3) We’ll loop in Legal/Finance for any non-standard contract language — see my note to Karthik and Marissa below.

Happy to jump on a 20-min procurement sync — what windows do they have next Tue?

Lauren — quick notes from Legal/Finance:

Finance (Marissa):
- Direct invoice: estimated 7–10 business days to set up vendor terms and accept PO for a first-time procurement. We require completed COA/SOW to accept the PO. For the pilot size you described, we can expedite to 3–5 business days if procurement provides a standard PO and tax form.
- Marketplace private offer: immediate from a Redwood provisioning perspective; invoice and payments are handled by AWS, which reduces our AR overhead. Note: customers sometimes record this as a third-party spend which can affect internal chargeback practices.

Legal (Karthik):
- Private offers are fine for the pilot; they do not change our underlying MSA terms (customer still bound by AWS/private offer terms + our standard EULA). If procurement requests alternate indemnity/PII clauses we will need a short MSA amendment.
- For larger/long-term deals, a direct MSA + SOW is recommended so we can negotiate SLAs and data handling clauses. Expect 2–4 review rounds on non-standard language.

Co-sell / incentives note: we can provide a summary of partner crediting cadence and estimated partner registration windows — that typically matters for sales credits but not for procurement acceptance.

If you want, I can pre-populate a DocuSign envelope with our standard MSA + SOW based on the COA template. I uploaded the draft templates to the shared Drive link in the packet and created a HubSpot task for RDW-20458.

— Karthik Iyer
